target: Static web build served from GitHub Pages (https://kranmal.github.io/lendly/) and a local copy of dist/
executiveSummary: Lendly has no backend. It is an Expo/React Native app exported as a static web site; all data lives in the browser (AsyncStorage, which is localStorage on web). A classic server load test (hundreds of virtual users) would only hammer GitHub Pages, which is not ours to load and which scales on its own. The real performance risks are on the client: a 1.1 MB (314 KB gzipped) single JavaScript bundle on first load, and data-handling code that gets slower as a user's lists grow (every list item recomputes all active loans, nothing is virtualised, and every change rewrites all stored data). The proposed strategy therefore measures (1) first-load speed and delivery, (2) client performance at 100 / 1,000 / 5,000 / 20,000 records, and (3) a small, polite k6 check of static delivery against a local copy only. Traffic-style load, stress and spike tests against the live site are explicitly out of scope.

system.stack: Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86 + react-native-web, expo-router (static output), React 19 with React Compiler
system.architecture: Client-only SPA, 3 prerendered routes (/, /items, /people) hydrating into one JS bundle. State is a module-level store with listeners (src/lib/store.ts).
system.dataStores: Browser localStorage via AsyncStorage: keys lendly:items, lendly:people, lendly:loans. No server database.
system.externalDeps: Google AdSense script and ad slot (src/components/ad-unit.tsx); GitHub Pages hosting and CDN (Fastly); deployed by .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml
system.notes: Mobile (iOS/Android) builds exist via Expo; this strategy covers the web build because that is what is deployed. Native runtime performance would need device profiling and is not covered.

findings.observation: One JS entry bundle of 1.1 MB raw, 314 KB gzipped (measured from dist/). No route-level splitting. Total dist is 1.3 MB.

Live site responds in 156 to 286 ms (TTFB, 3 sequential requests, Frankfurt edge), HTTP/2, gzip. HTML cache-control is max-age=600, so a returning visitor revalidates every 10 minutes. Cache headers for the hashed JS are not controllable on GitHub Pages.
AdSense script loads on every page and injects an ad slot; it adds network, main-thread cost and layout shift that we do not control. It must be excluded or isolated when measuring our own code.

For every item, getLoanForItem calls getActiveLoans, which filters, enriches (linear item and person lookups per loan) and sorts ALL loans. Cost per render grows roughly with items x loans x (items + people) and runs twice on the Items screen (filter and row render).
All lists use ScrollView with .map, so every row is mounted at once; there is no FlatList or virtualisation.
Every mutation rewrites all three localStorage keys with JSON.stringify of the full arrays, synchronously on the main thread (AsyncStorage on web). Cost is linear in total data size per tap.

On load the app reads and JSON.parses all three keys before the first meaningful render (loaded flag). A user with years of history pays this on every visit. localStorage is limited to about 5 MB per origin, which is a hard ceiling to test toward.
useNow ticks every 60 s and every mounted LoanRow subscribes, so each tick re-renders all visible rows. useStore re-renders every subscriber on any change.
There are no API endpoints, database, auth or queues to load test.
findings.evidence: package.json dependencies; src/ contains no fetch or API calls

journeys.name: First visit (cold)
steps: Hydrate, read localStorage, first meaningful render

workload.expectedConcurrentUsers: not applicable: the server work per user is a static file fetch
workload.basis: No analytics available to the analysis. Dataset sizes below are assumptions about plausible personal use.
assumptions: Typical user: 10 to 100 items, 5 to 30 people, 20 to 300 loans (assumed).
Heavy user: 1,000 items, 100 people, 5,000 loans (assumed upper realistic bound).
Extreme test point: 20,000 loans to find where the app breaks or localStorage fills (stress equivalent).
Test device: desktop Chromium with 4x CPU throttling to approximate a mid-range phone (assumed), plus unthrottled.

slos.metric: Largest Contentful Paint, cold load, 4x CPU throttle, simulated 4G
slos.rationale: Google 'good' threshold; also affects search ranking, which the SEO work targets.
Lighthouse 'good' threshold; reflects the 1.1 MB bundle parse cost.
Ad slot injection is the likely source.

slos.metric: Time to interactive list at 100 / 1,000 loans
slos.rationale: Assumed usability limits; to be confirmed by you.

slos.metric: Add-loan action (tap to UI updated), at 1,000 loans
Items tab render time at 1,000 items and 1,000 loans
Static delivery from local dist: p95 latency, error rate
slos.rationale: Sanity check of asset delivery with k6 against a local server only.

testPlan.purpose: Prove the harness works: serve dist locally, load the three routes, k6 fetches them once.
testPlan.why: Required first step for every later test.

testPlan.purpose: Measure LCP, TBT, CLS, bundle parse time, with and without the AdSense script.
testPlan.load: Single page loads, 10 repeats, throttled and unthrottled
testPlan.why: This is where the 1.1 MB bundle shows up; k6 cannot see render cost.

testPlan.purpose: Seed 100, 1,000, 5,000, 20,000 loans (with proportional items and people), then measure startup, tab render time, add-loan latency and mark-returned latency using the Performance API.
testPlan.passCriteria: Client SLOs above; report the dataset size where each SLO is first broken
testPlan.why: This is the realistic stress test for a client-only app and targets findings 4 to 6.

testPlan.purpose: Check static delivery of dist under concurrent fetches, e.g. 50 virtual users for 2 minutes.
testPlan.why: Cheap sanity check; note it measures the local static server, not GitHub Pages, so it says little about production.

testPlan.purpose: Find how many records fit before localStorage throws and what the app does when it does.
testPlan.passCriteria: App degrades gracefully (error handled, no data loss shown)
testPlan.why: Persist has no error handling for quota errors (src/lib/store.ts:36).

testPlan.purpose: Leave the app open for 1 hour with 1,000 loans and watch memory and the 60 s tick re-renders.
testPlan.why: Low risk; skip unless you want it.

environment.target: Local only: `npx expo export -p web` then a local static server on localhost, driven by Playwright (already in e2e-tests/) and k6. Live site: at most single read-only requests (as done during this analysis).
environment.dataNeeds: Synthetic generated items, people and loans injected into localStorage. No real data exists server-side.
safeguards: No load test against kranmal.github.io, GitHub Pages or AdSense (not ours, terms of service, no benefit).
k6 host guard allows localhost only.
AdSense is blocked in measurement runs unless the run is explicitly the 'with ads' variant.
No changes to the lendly source; findings only. The perf/ folder is added uncommitted.
monitoring: Chromium Performance API marks, long-task entries and JS heap size
k6 metrics for the local delivery check

tooling.tool: Playwright (already used in e2e-tests/) plus Lighthouse for the browser measurements, and k6 only for the local static-delivery check
tooling.why: The risks are in the browser, which k6 does not run. Playwright can seed localStorage, drive the UI and read performance entries. k6 adds little here but keeps the same harness and report as other projects.
tooling.alternatives: JMeter or Locust would only test the server and add nothing for a client-only app. k6 browser module is possible but less mature than Playwright for this.

risks.risk: Laptop CPU noise makes timings vary
risks.mitigation: 10 repeats, report median and p95, close other apps, same machine for before/after comparisons.

risks.risk: CPU throttling is only an approximation of a real phone
risks.mitigation: State this in the report; optionally confirm on a real device later.

risks.risk: Dataset assumptions may not match real use
risks.mitigation: Report results as a curve over dataset size, so you can read off your own number.

risks.risk: Local dist differs from the live deployment (base path /lendly, CDN)
risks.mitigation: Build with GH_PAGES_BASE_URL=/lendly as the deploy workflow does.

openQuestions: Do you have real usage numbers (visitors per day, device mix, typical number of items and loans)? Without them the dataset sizes are assumptions.
Which matters more: web (SEO, first load) or the mobile apps? This plan covers web only.
Are you happy to measure with the AdSense ad blocked by default, plus one 'with ads' run?
Are the proposed SLOs (LCP < 2.5 s, add-loan < 100 ms, Items tab < 1 s at 1,000 records) the right bar?
Is it OK for me to add the perf/ folder to the lendly repo (uncommitted, you decide whether to commit via a PR)?
notInScope: Load, stress or spike testing GitHub Pages or any live third-party service
Native iOS and Android runtime performance
Fixing the performance issues (findings are reported, not changed)
Server capacity planning: there is no server
